steps.title: Different origins on the right and left

pins.name: Right subclavian
pins.text: Arises from the brachiocephalic trunk.

pins.name: Left subclavian
pins.text: Arises from the aortic arch.

steps.title: One muscle divides the artery into three parts

pins.name: 1st part
pins.text: Medial to scalenus anterior.

pins.name: 2nd part
pins.text: Behind scalenus anterior.

pins.name: 3rd part
pins.text: Lateral to scalenus anterior.

pins.name: Scalenus anterior
pins.text: The translucent muscle is the landmark used to divide the artery.

steps.caption: Part colors are educational; their boundaries are approximate and follow the muscle position in this model.

steps.title: The artery continues as the axillary artery

pins.name: Subclavian â†’ Axillary
pins.text: At the outer border of the first rib, the subclavian ends and the axillary begins.

pins.name: Axillary artery
pins.text: The artery continues beyond this landmark.

steps.title: Three branches from the first part

pins.name: Vertebral artery
pins.text: A branch of the first part.

pins.name: Thyrocervical trunk
pins.text: The thyrocervical trunk arises from the first part.

pins.name: Internal thoracic artery
pins.text: Also called the internal mammary artery.

steps.title: The thyrocervical trunk gives three branches

pins.name: Inferior thyroid
pins.text: The inferior thyroid artery.

pins.name: Transverse cervical
pins.text: Also called the superficial cervical artery in the lecture.

pins.name: Suprascapular
pins.text: The suprascapular artery.

steps.title: Second-part branch: costocervical trunk

pins.name: Costo-cervical trunk
pins.text: Arises from the second part and gives the two branches shown.

pins.name: Superior intercostal
pins.text: Named the supreme intercostal artery in this model.

pins.name: Deep cervical
pins.text: The deep cervical artery.

steps.title: The third part may give no branches

pins.name: 3rd part
pins.text: May give the dorsal scapular artery, or may give no branches.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: The line points to the third part. The dorsal scapular artery is not a separate structure under this name in the model.

steps.title: Beginning and termination of the axillary artery

pins.name: Beginning
pins.text: Continues from the subclavian at the outer border of the first rib.

pins.name: Axillary â†’ Brachial
pins.text: Continues as the brachial artery at the lower border of teres major.

pins.name: Teres major
pins.text: The muscle associated with the termination landmark in the lecture.

steps.caption: The name transition in this general model may not match the muscle border in the lecture diagram exactly.

steps.title: Three parts around pectoralis minor

pins.name: 1st part
pins.text: From the outer border of the first rib to the upper border of pectoralis minor.

pins.name: 2nd part
pins.text: Behind pectoralis minor.

pins.name: 3rd part
pins.text: From the lower border of pectoralis minor to the lower border of teres major.

pins.name: Pectoralis minor
pins.text: The translucent muscle separates the parts of the artery.

steps.caption: Colors show approximate educational divisions around the projected muscle. The anatomical relations define the parts.

steps.title: The first part gives one branch

pins.name: 1st part â†’ Superior thoracic
pins.text: The superior thoracic artery is the only branch of the first part.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: The superior thoracic artery is shown in the diagram but is not a separate structure in this model.

steps.title: The second part gives two branches

pins.name: Thoraco-acromial
pins.text: One of the two branches of the second part.

pins.name: Lateral thoracic
pins.text: The other branch of the second part.

steps.title: Four branches of the thoraco-acromial artery

pins.name: Thoraco-acromial branches
pins.text: Clavicular, humeral, acromial and pectoral, as labeled in the lecture diagram.

pins.name: Pectoral branches
pins.text: The pectoral branches are represented here in the model.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: The diagram names all four branches; the model does not separate every branch.

steps.title: The third part gives three branches

pins.name: Subscapular
pins.text: The subscapular artery.

pins.name: Anterior circumflex humeral
pins.text: The anterior circumflex humeral artery.

pins.name: Posterior circumflex humeral
pins.text: The posterior circumflex humeral artery.

steps.title: The subscapular artery divides into two branches

pins.name: Circumflex scapular
pins.text: The circumflex branch around the scapula.

pins.name: Thoracodorsal
pins.text: The thoracodorsal branch.

steps.title: Shoulder anastomosis: subclavian contributions

pins.name: Suprascapular
pins.text: Participates in the anastomosis around the shoulder.

pins.name: Deep branch of superficial cervical
pins.text: The lecture calls this the deep branch of the superficial cervical artery.

steps.title: Shoulder anastomosis: axillary contributions

pins.name: Circumflex scapular
pins.text: The branch of the subscapular artery participating in the anastomosis.

pins.name: Anterior circumflex humeral
pins.text: One of the participating circumflex humeral arteries.

pins.name: Posterior circumflex humeral
pins.text: The posterior circumflex humeral artery also participates.

steps.title: From the arm to the two forearm arteries

pins.name: Brachial artery
pins.text: Terminates opposite the neck of the radius.

pins.name: Radial artery
pins.text: One of the two terminal branches.

pins.name: Ulnar artery
pins.text: The other terminal branch.

steps.title: Two veins accompany the artery

pins.name: Brachial artery
pins.text: Descends in the anterior compartment of the arm.

pins.name: Two brachial veins
pins.text: Two brachial veins accompany it.

steps.title: Median nerve: begin in the upper arm

pins.name: Median nerve â€” upper arm
pins.text: The median nerve is lateral to the artery here.

pins.name: Brachial artery
pins.text: Observe the nerve's position relative to the artery.

steps.title: At mid-arm, the nerve crosses anteriorly

pins.name: Median nerve â€” crossing
pins.text: Crosses in front of the brachial artery from lateral to medial.

pins.name: Brachial artery
pins.text: The artery lies behind the nerve during the crossing.

steps.title: After crossing, the nerve remains medial

pins.name: Median nerve â€” lower arm
pins.text: Remains medial to the artery down to the cubital fossa.

pins.name: Brachial artery
pins.text: Follow this relationship to the cubital fossa.

steps.title: Ulnar nerve in the upper arm

pins.name: Ulnar nerve
pins.text: Lies medial to the brachial artery in the upper arm.

pins.name: Brachial artery
pins.text: The artery is the reference for the nerve's position.

steps.title: Profunda brachii: the largest brachial branch

pins.name: Profunda brachii
pins.text: The largest branch of the brachial artery; named deep brachial artery here.

pins.name: Radial nerve
pins.text: Accompanies the artery in the spiral groove.

steps.title: Termination of the profunda brachii

pins.name: Anterior descending
pins.text: One terminal branch; named radial collateral in the model.

pins.name: Posterior descending
pins.text: The other branch; named middle collateral in the model.

steps.title: Branches supplying muscle and bone

pins.name: Muscular branches
pins.text: Supply the muscles of the anterior compartment of the arm.

pins.name: Nutrient artery to humerus
pins.text: The brachial artery also gives the nutrient artery to the humerus.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: The lines link the explanation to the parent artery and bone. The small branches are not separately modeled.

steps.title: The two ulnar collateral branches

pins.name: Superior ulnar collateral
pins.text: Accompanies the ulnar nerve.

pins.name: Inferior ulnar collateral
pins.text: The inferior ulnar collateral branch.

pins.name: Ulnar nerve
pins.text: The nerve accompanying the superior branch.

steps.title: Two brachial branches at the neck of the radius

pins.name: Radial â€” smaller
pins.text: The smaller terminal branch.

pins.name: Ulnar â€” larger
pins.text: The larger terminal branch.

steps.title: Radial artery along the lateral forearm

pins.name: Radial artery
pins.text: Descends on the lateral side of the forearm, deep to brachioradialis.

pins.name: Brachioradialis
pins.text: The muscle is translucent so the artery beneath it remains visible.

steps.title: The pulse site at the wrist

pins.name: Radial pulse
pins.text: Becomes superficial at the wrist. Its pulse is felt lateral to the flexor carpi radialis tendon.

pins.name: Flexor carpi radialis
pins.text: Compare the muscle's course with the artery at the wrist.

steps.title: In the anatomical snuff box

pins.name: Radial artery
pins.text: Passes through the anatomical snuff box and lies on the scaphoid.

pins.name: Scaphoid
pins.text: The scaphoid bone lies beneath the artery at this location.

steps.title: The route into the palm

pins.name: First dorsal interosseous
pins.text: Passes between the two heads of the first dorsal interosseous muscle.

pins.name: Adductor pollicis
pins.text: Then passes between the two heads of adductor pollicis to reach the palm.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: This sequence follows the lecture. Dashed lines connect the explanation to the available vessel or muscle.

steps.title: Radial branches in the forearm and wrist

pins.name: Forearm branches
pins.text: Muscular branches and the radial recurrent branch.

pins.name: Carpal & palmar branches
pins.text: Anterior and posterior carpal branches, and the superficial palmar branch; ends as the deep palmar arch.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: Branches not separately modeled are shown in the lecture diagram.

steps.title: Branches to the thumb and index finger

pins.name: Princeps pollicis
pins.text: A radial branch supplying the side of the thumb.

pins.name: Radialis indicis
pins.text: A radial branch supplying the lateral side of the index finger.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: These branches are not separate in the model. Lines indicate the parent vessel; the diagram shows their distribution.

steps.title: Ulnar artery along the medial forearm

pins.name: Ulnar artery
pins.text: Descends medially in the forearm, deep to flexor carpi ulnaris and lateral to the ulnar nerve.

pins.name: Ulnar nerve
pins.text: Medial to the artery in the forearm.

pins.name: Flexor carpi ulnaris
pins.text: The muscle lies superficial to the artery.
pins.target: Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.r

context: Humeral head of flexor carpi ulnaris.r
Ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris.r

steps.title: Entering the hand above the flexor retinaculum

pins.name: Ulnar artery at wrist
pins.text: Enters the hand superficial to the flexor retinaculum.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: The flexor retinaculum is not a separate displayed layer; the lecture states this relationship.

steps.title: Branches of the ulnar artery

pins.name: Forearm branches
pins.text: Muscular; anterior and posterior ulnar recurrent; common interosseous.

pins.name: Wrist & hand branches
pins.text: Anterior and posterior carpal; deep palmar branch; ends as the superficial palmar arch.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.title: Interosseous division and recurrent branch

pins.name: Common interosseous
pins.text: Divides into anterior and posterior interosseous arteries.

pins.name: Posterior interosseous
pins.text: Gives the interosseous recurrent artery.

pins.name: Interosseous recurrent
pins.text: Named recurrent interosseous artery in the model.

steps.caption: The anterior interosseous artery is not separately modeled; its origin is explained in the label.

steps.title: Arterial supply of the fingers

pins.name: Radial territory
pins.text: Mainly supplies the thumb and lateral side of the index finger.

pins.name: Ulnar territory
pins.text: Supplies the medial side of the index finger and the remaining three digits.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: These are the lecture's supply territories. The lines do not mark skin-territory boundaries on the model.

steps.title: Deep arch: radial origin, ulnar completion

pins.name: Deep palmar arch
pins.text: Begins as a continuation of the radial artery after it enters the palm.

pins.name: Medial completion
pins.text: Completed medially by the deep palmar branch of the ulnar artery.

steps.caption: The completing branch is not separate in the model; the label explains its connection to the arch.

steps.title: The deep arch curves medially

pins.name: Curves medially
pins.text: The arch curves toward the medial side.

pins.name: Depth relations
pins.text: Deep to the long flexor tendons; superficial to the metacarpal bones and interosseous muscles.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.title: Surface level of the deep palmar arch

pins.name: Proximal border of extended thumb
pins.text: Lies at the level of the proximal border of the extended thumb.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: The diagram shows the extended-thumb position used to identify the surface level.

steps.title: Palmar metacarpal branches

pins.name: Palmar metacarpal arteries
pins.text: Branches from the deep arch toward the fingers, as shown in the diagram.

pins.name: Deep palmar arch
pins.text: The arch from which they arise.

steps.title: Superficial arch: ulnar origin, radial completion

pins.name: Superficial palmar arch
pins.text: Begins as a continuation of the ulnar artery after it enters the palm.

pins.name: Lateral completion
pins.text: Completed laterally by the superficial palmar branch of the radial artery.

steps.caption: The completing branch is not separate in the model; the label explains its connection to the arch.

steps.title: The superficial arch curves laterally

pins.name: Curves laterally
pins.text: The arch curves toward the lateral side.

pins.name: Depth relations
pins.text: Deep to the palmar aponeurosis and superficial to the long flexor tendons.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.title: Surface level of the superficial palmar arch

pins.name: Distal border of extended thumb
pins.text: Lies at the level of the distal border of the fully extended thumb.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: Compare the diagrams: the superficial arch is at the distal border; the deep arch is at the proximal border.

steps.title: Digital arteries from the palm

pins.name: Common palmar digital
pins.text: The common palmar digital arteries.

pins.name: Proper palmar digital
pins.text: The proper palmar digital arteries running along the sides of the fingers.

steps.title: A connection above and below the elbow

pins.name: From above
pins.text: Branches of the brachial and profunda brachii arteries.

pins.name: From below
pins.text: Branches of the radial and ulnar arteries.

steps.title: In front of the medial epicondyle

pins.name: Inferior ulnar collateral
pins.text: Anastomoses with the anterior ulnar recurrent artery in front of the medial epicondyle.

pins.name: Anterior ulnar recurrent
pins.text: The model does not separate the anterior and posterior branches; see their positions in the diagram.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.title: Behind the medial epicondyle

pins.name: Superior ulnar collateral
pins.text: Anastomoses with the posterior ulnar recurrent artery behind the medial epicondyle.

pins.name: Posterior ulnar recurrent
pins.text: Meets it from below, as the diagram shows.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.title: In front of the lateral epicondyle

pins.name: Anterior descending
pins.text: A profunda brachii branch joining the radial recurrent artery in front of the lateral epicondyle.

pins.name: Radial recurrent
pins.text: Not separately modeled; its position and connection appear in the diagram.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.title: Behind the lateral epicondyle

pins.name: Posterior descending
pins.text: A profunda brachii branch; named middle collateral here.

pins.name: Interosseous recurrent
pins.text: Joins the posterior descending branch behind the lateral epicondyle.

steps.title: The anterior carpal arch

pins.name: Anterior carpal arch
pins.text: At the front of the wrist: anterior carpal branches of the radial and ulnar arteries join.
pins.target: Palmar carpal branch of radial artery.r

focus: Palmar carpal branch of radial artery.r

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: The model shows the available radial carpal branch; the complete anterior arch is not a separate structure.

steps.title: The posterior carpal arch

pins.name: Posterior carpal arch
pins.text: At the back of the wrist: posterior carpal branches of the radial and ulnar arteries join.

pins.name: Ulnar dorsal carpal branch
pins.text: One of the participating branches shown here.
pins.target: Dorsal carpal branch of ulnar artery.r

focus: Dorsal carpal branch of ulnar artery.r

steps.title: From digital veins to the dorsal arch

pins.name: Digital veins
pins.text: Palmar and dorsal digital veins join.

pins.name: Dorsal venous arch
pins.text: They form the dorsal venous arch, named dorsal venous network in the model.

steps.title: Cephalic vein: the lateral continuation

pins.name: Lateral continuation
pins.text: Begins as the lateral continuation of the dorsal venous arch.

pins.name: Lateral forearm
pins.text: Ascends along the lateral side of the forearm.

steps.title: Draining into the axillary vein

pins.name: Clavipectoral triangle
pins.text: The cephalic vein passes through the clavipectoral triangle.

pins.name: Clavipectoral fascia â†’ Axillary vein
pins.text: Pierces the clavipectoral fascia to drain into the axillary vein.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: The fascia is not modeled as a separate layer; the lecture shows the passage.

steps.title: Basilic vein: the medial continuation

pins.name: Medial continuation
pins.text: The medial continuation of the dorsal venous arch.

pins.name: Medial forearm
pins.text: Ascends along the medial side of the forearm.

steps.title: From the basilic to the axillary vein

pins.name: Deep fascia
pins.text: According to the lecture, it pierces the deep fascia at mid-arm.

pins.name: Basilic + brachial veins
pins.text: Then joins the brachial veins to form the axillary vein.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: This preserves the lecture's wording. The union in the general model may differ from the diagram.

steps.title: An oblique bridge across the cubital fossa

pins.name: Median cubital vein
pins.text: Passes obliquely across the cubital fossa, connecting the cephalic and basilic veins.

pins.name: Intravenous injection
pins.text: The lecture identifies this as the most commonly used vein for intravenous injection.

steps.title: Median vein of the forearm

pins.name: Median antebrachial vein
pins.text: May drain into the basilic vein, cephalic vein, or both.

steps.caption: The model shows one arrangement; the lecture lists all three drainage possibilities.

steps.title: Venae comitantes: two veins per artery

pins.name: Radial veins
pins.text: Two veins accompany the radial artery.

pins.name: Ulnar veins
pins.text: Two veins accompany the ulnar artery.

pins.name: Brachial veins
pins.text: Two veins accompany the brachial artery. These are deep veins.

steps.title: Forearm veins unite as brachial veins

pins.name: Radial + ulnar veins
pins.text: The veins accompanying the two forearm arteries unite.

pins.name: Brachial venae comitantes
pins.text: They form the veins accompanying the brachial artery.

steps.title: Sympathetic supply: preganglionic fibers

pins.name: Sympathetic supply â€” T2â€“T8
pins.text: Preganglionic fibers arise from T2 to T8.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: These levels and microscopic fibers are not displayed. The line only indicates the plexus region for orientation.

steps.title: Sources of postganglionic fibers

pins.name: Postganglionic fibers
pins.text: Middle cervical, inferior cervical, first thoracic, or stellate ganglia.

diagram.note: Original lecture diagram. Dashed lines indicate the parent vessel for details not separately modeled.

steps.caption: These are the sources listed in the lecture. No estimated markers are placed on ganglia not separately modeled.

steps.title: Plexus nerves carry fibers to the vessels

pins.name: Brachial plexus nerves
pins.text: Distribute postganglionic fibers to accompany arteries and veins.

pins.name: Along nerves and vessels
pins.text: The model shows large nerves and vessels; sympathetic fibers themselves are microscopic.
